A stray footnote number '1' in 3.476 is left out. 'elisa ... dextra' (3.482) is uncertain: the hand struck powerless, or the balsam squeezed out of it.

nodes.text: of the ruler of Aeneas' people lies prostrate at the courts of Christ,
and the supreme lord adores the standard of the cross.
Yet out of all the princes there was not lacking one —
when I was a boy, as I remember — a leader most valiant in arms,
a maker of laws too, most renowned in speech and in action,
a counsellor for his country, but no counsellor for keeping
religion, a lover of three hundred thousand gods.
Faithless to God, though not faithless to the world, he
bowed his imperial head before the feet of Minerva
made of clay, and licked the sandals of Juno, at the soles
of Hercules grovelled, coated Diana's knees with wax,
and even lowered his brow to Apollo in plaster
or fumed the horse of Pollux with burning entrails.
It happened that, sacrificing, he was appeasing Hecate with much blood;
there, to be struck by the priests' festal axes,
lines of cows had been set waiting, and the heifers, on their bound
brows garlanded, were shaded by twisted cypress.
And now, with the knife driven in, he had laid the entrails open —
the old man in his fillets, as custom is — and with bloody hands
was handling the organs, quivering in the cold of death,
and the last pulses of life in the cooling heart
the cunning interpreter was marking by their count and their ending,
when suddenly amid the rites the priest cries out,
pale: ‘Look, what am I doing? A greater, best of kings, a greater
power, I know not what, has come upon our altars
than foaming bowls of milk could withstand,
or the blood of slaughtered cattle, holy boughs, and garlands.
I see the summoned shades scattering far away;
terrified Persephone turns her steps back,
her torches quenched, fleeing, her whip trailing;
the secret murmur does nothing, the Thessalian spells
avail nothing, no victim calls back the troubled ghosts.
Do you not see how in the cooling censers the fire
withers, how the coal grows sluggish under grey ash?
Look, the palace attendant, to keep hold of the bowl,
has no strength; the balsam drips from his stricken right hand;
and the flamen himself wonders to see his laurels from his crown
slip away, and the victim eludes the faltering steel.
Surely some one of the Christ-worshippers has crept in
here, among the young men; at this race of men the fillet trembles, and every
couch of the gods. Let him who is washed and anointed keep far off;
let fair Proserpina return, her rites restored.’
He spoke, and collapses bloodless; and, as though he saw
Christ himself threatening with his thunderbolt bared,
the prince too, breathless, his diadem laid aside,
turns pale and looks round at those standing by, to see whether some nursling
of the chrism had signed his temples with the wood traced on them,
who with his brow had thrown the Zoroastrian whispers into confusion.
An armour-bearer from the troop of golden-haired youths,
a guard of the purple-clad side, is caught, one alone,
and does not deny it, and his jewelled spear with its double iron
he throws down, and confesses that he bears the sign of Christ.
The prince leapt up in fear, the priest laid low,
fleeing the marble shrine with no one following him,
while the terror-struck guard, forgetting their lord, lift their upturned
faces to heaven and call upon Jesus.
Now are you sorry for the deed? Now do you repent? See, here for you is Christ,
